questions.question: The perimeter of a circle is 44 cm. What is its radius?

solution.content: **Use the circumference formula:** $C = 2\pi r$. Given $C = 44$ cm and $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$: $$44 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = \frac{44r}{7}$$
**Solve for $r$:** $$r = \frac{44 \times 7}{44} = 7 \text{ cm}$$

questions.answer: The radius of the circle is 7 cm.
questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** When the circumference is a multiple of 44, the radius is often a whole number using π = 22/7.

questions.question: Calculate, correct to 3 significant figures, the circumference of a circle with: **(i)** radius 7 cm **(ii)** radius 10 cm **(iii)** radius 12 cm.

solution.content: **(i) Radius 7 cm:** $$C = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 44 \text{ cm}$$
**(ii) Radius 10 cm:** $$C = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10 = \frac{440}{7} = 62.857\ldots \approx 62.9 \text{ cm}$$
**(iii) Radius 12 cm:** $$C = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 12 = \frac{528}{7} = 75.428\ldots \approx 75.4 \text{ cm}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** To 3 significant figures, 62.857… becomes 62.9 and 75.428… becomes 75.4.

questions.question: Calculate the length of the arc of a circle if: **(i)** the radius is 3.5 cm and the angle at the centre is $60°$, and **(ii)** the radius is 6.3 m and the angle at the centre is $120°$.

solution.content: **Use the arc length formula:** $L = \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$.
**(i) $r = 3.5$ cm, $\theta = 60°$:** $$L = \frac{60}{360} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 = \frac{1}{6} \times 22 = \frac{11}{3} \approx 3.67 \text{ cm}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** The arc length is the fraction θ/360 of the full circumference.

questions.question: Find the perimeter of a sector (i.e., the curved portion as well as the two straight portions) of a circle of radius 14 cm and sector angle $75°$.

solution.content: **Find the arc length:** $$L = \frac{75}{360} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 = \frac{75}{360} \times 88 = \frac{5}{24} \times 88 = \frac{55}{3} \text{ cm}$$
**Add the two radii:** $$\text{Perimeter} = L + 2r = \frac{55}{3} + 2 \times 14 = \frac{55}{3} + 28 = \frac{55 + 84}{3} = \frac{139}{3} \approx 46.33 \text{ cm}$$

questions.answer: The perimeter of the sector is 139/3 cm ≈ 46.33 cm.
questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** A sector's perimeter includes the arc plus the two straight radii.

questions.question: Find the perimeters of the following shapes (taking the arcs to be quarter or half or three-quarters of a circle, as appropriate) (Fig. 6.14i to 6.14ix): **(i)** 60 m, 80 m **(ii)** 8 cm, 12 cm **(iii)** 10 cm **(iv)** 12 cm **(v)** 14 cm **(vi)** 28 cm **(vii)** 8 cm, 6 cm **(viii)** 4 cm, 4 cm, 4 cm **(ix)** 10 cm, 10 cm

solution.content: **(i) Rectangle with semicircular ends (60 m diameter, 80 m straight):** Two straight parts of 80 m each plus two semicircles of diameter 60 m (together one full circle): $$80 + 80 + \pi \times 60 = 160 + \frac{22}{7} \times 60 = 160 + \frac{1320}{7} = 348.57 \text{ m}$$
**(ii) Outer semicircle diameter 12 cm, inner semicircle diameter 8 cm, straight parts 2 cm + 2 cm:** $$\pi(6) + \pi(4) + 4 = 10\pi + 4 = \frac{220}{7} + 4 = 35.43 \text{ cm}$$
**(iii) Four semicircles, each with diameter 10 cm (radius 5 cm):** $$4 \times \pi \times 5 = 20\pi = \frac{440}{7} = 62.86 \text{ cm}$$
**(iv) Three semicircles, each with diameter 12 cm (radius 6 cm):** $$3 \times \pi \times 6 = 18\pi = \frac{396}{7} = 56.57 \text{ cm}$$
**(v) Four semicircles (diameter 14 cm, radius 7 cm) and four quarter circles (radius 14 cm):** $$4 \times \pi \times 7 + 4 \times \frac{1}{2}\pi \times 14 = 28\pi + 28\pi = 56\pi = 176 \text{ cm}$$
**(vi) Large semicircle (diameter 28 cm, radius 14 cm) and four small semicircles (diameter 7 cm, radius 3.5 cm):** $$\pi(14) + 4 \times \pi(3.5) = 14\pi + 14\pi = 28\pi = 88 \text{ cm}$$

**(vii) Semicircles on the sides of a right triangle (perpendicular sides 8 cm and 6 cm):** Hypotenuse $= \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$ cm. Perimeter $= \pi(3) + \pi(4) + \pi(5) = 12\pi = \frac{264}{7} = 37.71$ cm.

**(viii) Large semicircle (diameter 12 cm, radius 6 cm) and three small semicircles (diameter 4 cm, radius 2 cm):** $$\pi(6) + 3 \times \pi(2) = 6\pi + 6\pi = 12\pi = \frac{264}{7} = 37.71 \text{ cm}$$

**(ix) Large semicircle (diameter 20 cm, radius 10 cm) and two small semicircles (diameter 10 cm, radius 5 cm):** $$\pi(10) + 2 \times \pi(5) = 10\pi + 10\pi = 20\pi = \frac{440}{7} = 62.86 \text{ cm}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** Two semicircles with the same diameter make one full circle, so combine them before multiplying by π.

questions.question: If the diameter of a car tyre is 56 cm, then: **(i)** How far does the car need to travel for the tyre to complete one revolution? **(ii)** How many revolutions does the tyre make if the car travels 10 km?

solution.content: **(i) Distance in one revolution = circumference:** $$C = 2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 28 = 176 \text{ cm}$$
**(ii) Convert 10 km to cm:** $$10 \text{ km} = 10 \times 1000 \times 100 = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ cm}$$
**Find the number of revolutions:** $$\frac{1{,}000{,}000}{176} = 5681.82 \approx 5682 \text{ revolutions}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** Distance travelled = number of revolutions × circumference.

questions.question: Find the total perimeter of all the petals in each of the given flowers. **(i)** A square of side 14 cm with arcs centred at the midpoints of the sides. **(ii)** A regular hexagon of side 42 cm with arcs centred at the vertices.

solution.content: **(i) Square of side 14 cm:** Each petal is formed by two quarter circles whose centres are the midpoints of the sides. Radius $= \frac{14}{2} = 7$ cm. Each petal consists of 2 quarter circles = 1 semicircle. With 4 petals, total arcs = 4 semicircles = 2 full circles: $$\text{Perimeter} = 2 \times 2\pi r = 4\pi r = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 88 \text{ cm}$$

**(ii) Regular hexagon of side 42 cm:** Each petal is formed by arcs of circles with radius 42 cm. There are 6 petals, each with 2 arcs of $60°$ (total angle per petal $= 120°$). Total angle for all petals $= 6 \times 120° = 720° = 2$ full circles: $$\text{Perimeter} = 2 \times 2\pi r = 4\pi r = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 42 = 528 \text{ cm}$$

questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** Count the total angle swept by all the arcs — if it equals 720°, that is exactly two full circles.

questions.question: The ratio of the perimeters of two circles is 5 : 4. What is the ratio of their radii?

solution.content: **Write the ratio of perimeters:** Let the radii be $R$ and $r$. $$2\pi R : 2\pi r = 5 : 4$$

questions.answer: The ratio of their radii is 5 : 4.
questions.notes: **Exam Tip:** Since C = 2πr, the circumference is proportional to the radius, so the ratio of circumferences equals the ratio of radii.
